meta.descripcion: In-browser simulation of a reply bot (text, photo and voice note) and four proactive bots, with fictional data and the architecture of real projects. Demo by Ramiro Bales.
cinta.texto: Demo by Ramiro Bales · Simulated in your browser with fictional data. The architecture is the one from real projects.

intro.titulo: Bots that answer with data and send alerts on their own.
intro.texto: This is a sports staff's bot: it takes text, photos and voice notes, and answers with the squad's data. Send it something and watch, in the panel, what happens inside each message.
acc.foto.que: reads the table, flags what's unclear

aviso.texto: There's no server, model or live bot: everything runs in your browser and nothing you type leaves this page. The club, the players and their data are made up. What's real is the architecture: the one behind the bots I built for AthleteIQ, Cathedra and Fortal.
chat.campo: Type a question for the bot
voz.transcripcion: Is Ferraro fit to play on Saturday?
foto.alt: Photo of a printed GPS report with six rows; one figure is smudged.
q.riesgo: Who is at risk from load this week?
r.bienvenida: Hi. I'm the staff bot for Ventisca RL (a fictional club). Ask me about load, availability, wellness or GPS for the {n} players. I take text, photos and voice notes.
r.riesgo.intro: {n} players are over the load threshold this week (acute:chronic ratio of {u} or more):
r.riesgo.item: {nombre} ({pos}): {acwr}. {carga} AU this week against a {prom} average over the previous four.
r.riesgo.item2: {nombre} ({pos}): {acwr}. {carga} AU this week against a {prom} average over the previous four. Also: wellness {b} out of 5 and {s} h of sleep.
r.riesgo.sug: Suggestion: cut Thursday's volume and check them again on Friday. The call is the staff's.
r.riesgo.fuente: Source: load sheet, week 14 · Tuesday's wellness survey.
r.disp.restriccion: {nombre}: available with restrictions. {nota} Load {acwr}; sprint at {pct}% of his average.
r.disp.apto: {nombre}: available, no restrictions from the medical staff. Load {acwr}; wellness {b} out of 5.
r.disp.decide: Whether he plays is the staff's call; this is what the data says.
r.disp.fuente: Source: Monday's medical report · GPS from sessions 12 to 14.
r.ficha: {nombre}, {pos}. Load this week: {acwr} ({carga} AU). Wellness {b} out of 5 and {s} h of sleep. Medical report: {estado}.
r.ficha.fuente: Source: load sheet, week 14 · Monday's medical report · Tuesday's wellness survey.
r.foto.intro: I read {n} rows from today's report. Worth a look:
r.foto.sprint: {nombre}: {v} m of sprinting against a {p} average (+{pct}%).
r.foto.duda: One figure is hard to read: {nombre}, {a} or {b} km? I won't save it until you confirm.
r.foto.guardado: The other {n} rows are already in the week {s} sheet.
r.foto.fuente: Source: the photo you sent · averages from the last four weeks.
r.confirma: Done: {nombre}, {v} km. I saved the row in the week {s} sheet.
r.fuera: I don't have that. The club loaded training load, GPS, medical reports and wellness; contracts and salaries aren't there, and I won't guess.
r.fuera.regla: Rule: if the data isn't there, say so.
r.gps: Send me the photo or a screenshot of the GPS report (with the paperclip) and I'll read it.
r.hola: Hi. I can answer about load, availability, wellness and GPS for the {n} players on file. Send me text, a photo or a voice note.
r.nose: I can't find that in the squad data and I'd rather not guess. I can answer about load, availability, wellness and GPS for the {n} players on file.
r.limite: This chat has reached today's limit of {max} queries; it resets at midnight. If it's urgent, message the strength and conditioning coach.
r.cache.nota: From cache: same question, same data.
nota.ferraro: He returned to full training on Monday after a left hamstring complaint, and the doctor asked to limit him to 60 minutes.
nota.melgarejo: Right ankle sprain; the doctor expects him back in two weeks.
traza.nota: In the real project every step goes into a log: what came in, what data was used, which rule applied and what went out.
p.entrada.texto: #{id} arrived: text, from the staff chat.
p.entrada.dup: #{id} arrived again: the channel retries when a reply is slow.
p.dup.frena: #{id} was already processed: it's dropped and not answered twice.
p.limite.ok: Query {n} of {max} today for this chat.
p.limite.frena: All {max} of today's queries are used: no model call; the user is told and pointed to a person.
p.prep.foto: Image read: {n} rows, one of them unclear.
p.cache.hit: This question was already answered and the data hasn't changed: the reply comes from cache.
p.cache.miss: No stored reply for this question with this data.
p.cache.nuevo: Not applicable: this is new data, not a repeated question.
p.cache.noaplica: Not applicable to this kind of message.
p.datos.riesgo: Load sheet and wellness survey for the {n} players. Over the threshold: {m}.
p.datos.jugador: Load sheet, medical report and GPS for {nombre}.
p.datos.foto: Four-week averages for the {n} players in the report. Out of the ordinary:
p.datos.fuera: Looked for contracts and salaries: they aren't in the data on file.
p.datos.nose: Nothing to look up: the question doesn't match anything on file.
p.datos.cache: Not needed: the stored reply already used them.
p.modelo.reglas: Rules: answer only from squad data, name the source and leave the decision to the staff. In this demo, a local template stands in for the model.
p.modelo.foto: Rule applied: an unclear figure isn't saved; the bot asks.
p.modelo.confirma: Rule applied: a figure confirmed by a person is saved and acknowledged.
p.modelo.fuera: Rule applied: if the data isn't there, say so; don't estimate.
p.modelo.nose: Rule applied: no data, no made-up answer; offer what is available.
p.modelo.cache: Not called: the reply came from cache.
p.resp.ok: Sent with its source and saved to the chat history ({n} messages).
p.resp.limite: Limit notice sent, at no cost.
p.resp.sinfuente: Sent and saved to the chat history ({n} messages).

pro.titulo: Four bots that work without anyone asking.
pro.intro: A clock or a calendar wakes them up, they read what they need to read and alert only when there's something new. Move the time or play the day. Messages, thresholds and data are examples; the kind of bot and its architecture are real.
ficha.todavia: It hasn't run yet: it's scheduled for {h}.

ev.noticias.regla: Alert only on what's new and relevant, never repeating what was already sent.

marca.titulo: Round-the-clock answers and alerts nobody has to remember to ask for.
marca.intro: What you see above with a sports squad works just as well for a store, a sales team or a support desk: the data changes, the architecture doesn't.
gana1.t: 24/7 answers from the brand's own data
gana1.p: It answers at 3 a.m. with the same information as your best salesperson, by text, photo or voice. If the data isn't there, it says so and hands off to a person.
gana2.p: Competitor prices, stock-outs, deadlines or opportunities: the bot checks at the set time and reports only what's new, without repeating what it already sent.
gana3.p: There's a record of what came in, what data was used, which rule applied and what went out. If an answer is wrong, you know why and fix the rule instead of guessing.
gana4.p: Caching avoids paying twice for the same answer, deduplication avoids replying twice to the same message and a per-chat limit caps spending. The real radar costs US$0.18 per run.
usos.titulo: Where I'd put it in a brand
uso1.p: The customer sends a photo of the receipt or asks about an order; the bot looks up the status and answers, or passes it to a person with the summary ready.
uso2.p: Competitor price tracking every morning and a radar for tenders, sponsors or new clients that never repeats what you've already seen.
uso3.p: Voice notes from the warehouse or the field that get transcribed and logged into the sheet automatically, with a flag when something isn't clear.
como.titulo: Two paths: when someone writes and when nobody does.
como.intro: This is the architecture of the bots I built for AthleteIQ (Telegram replies, a prototype news brief and radar), Cathedra (exam and assignment reminders) and Fortal (workout push alerts). I built them with AI-assisted development: I defined what each piece does and why, and I verified the result.
caja.canal.p: Telegram notifies the server with an HTTP call for every message: text, photo or voice.
caja.dup.p: Every message carries a number. If the channel resends it, it's processed only once.
caja.lim.p: A quota per chat per day: it protects cost and stops abuse.
caja.prep.p: Voice is transcribed and photos are read before the answer is worked out.
caja.cache.p: Same question, same data: same answer, without paying again.
caja.modelo.p: It answers only from the client's data and the chat history, and names the source.
caja.resp.p: It goes back to the chat in the asker's language and stays in the history.
caja.reloj.p: A fixed time or a calendar date wakes the bot up.
caja.fuentes.p: It reads industry news, public sources, the calendar or the day's workout.
caja.novedad.p: It compares against what was already sent and drops repeats and low-relevance items.
caja.aviso.p: A message or push notification, only if something worthwhile is left.

dec1.i: The channel retries when the bot is slow.
dec1.t: Deduplicate by message number before anything else.
dec1.no: I ruled out trusting that each message arrives once: with a slow reply, the user gets two and you pay twice.
dec2.i: A repeated alert stops being read.
dec2.t: The radar keeps what it already sent and rejects repeats.
dec2.no: I ruled out sending everything it finds: within a week the channel is noise.
dec3.i: A misread figure is worse than none.
dec3.t: What's missing or unclear gets asked about or stated.
dec3.no: I ruled out letting the bot fill the gap with the most likely value: in a medical report or a price, guessing is expensive.
afuera1: There's no language model: replies are templates over made-up data, so it understands few questions.
afuera2: The audio and the photo are samples; you can't upload your own.
afuera3: Cathedra's voice assistant and oral exam aren't here.
afuera4: The 20-query quota belongs to this demo; in each project the limit is set to fit its use.
afuera5: I tested keyboard, focus and structure; I didn't test with users or with real screen readers.
